record.paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
record.original_question: How important is active-galactic-nucleus feedback in shaping the observed relations between black-hole mass and host-galaxy properties in nearby and high-redshift quasars?

evidence.quote: Observationally established correlations between black hole mass and host galaxy structural/dynamical properties (like the MBH − σ∗ relation) give support to the idea of an intimate link between the growth of black holes (BHs) and their host galaxies.
Clear signs of AGN feedback have been observed in nearby and high redshift quasars, but their importance in shaping the black hole mass – host galaxy relations is still under debate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supermassive black holes residing at the centers of galaxies hosting active galactic nuclei (AGN). Let M_BH denote the mass of the central black hole, and let host-galaxy properties include the stellar velocity dispersion σ_* of the bulge, the bulge stellar mass M_bulge, and bulge luminosity. Empirical correlations such as the M_BH–σ_* relation are observed across the local universe and, with greater uncertainty, at high redshift in quasar samples. "AGN feedback" refers to the energy and momentum injected into the surrounding interstellar and circumgalactic medium by accretion onto the central black hole, in radiative (quasar) and kinetic (jet/outflow) modes, which can heat, expel, or regulate gas available for both star formation and continued black-hole accretion.

Determine quantitatively the role of AGN feedback in establishing and maintaining the observed scaling relations between M_BH and host-galaxy properties (in particular M_BH–σ_*, M_BH–M_bulge, and M_BH–L_bulge) for both nearby (z ≈ 0) and high-redshift (z ≳ 1) quasars. Specifically: (i) is AGN feedback a necessary causal driver of the normalization and slope of these relations, or do they instead arise predominantly from hierarchical merger averaging or from a common gas supply regulating both BH growth and bulge growth; (ii) how does the relative importance of radiative versus kinetic feedback modes depend on redshift and on host-galaxy mass; and (iii) quantify the predicted redshift evolution of the normalization of the M_BH–σ_* and M_BH–M_bulge relations under self-regulated AGN-feedback models, and compare with the evolution required by observations.
artifact.category_tag: AGN feedback and black-hole–host-galaxy scaling relations
artifact.status_search_result: The quantitative role of AGN feedback in shaping the M_BH–σ_* and M_BH–M_bulge relations remains an actively debated open problem in extragalactic astrophysics. Recent reviews (e.g., Kormendy & Ho 2013; Heckman & Best 2014; Harrison 2017; Harrison & Ramos Almeida 2024) emphasize that while AGN-driven outflows are ubiquitously detected in nearby and high-z quasars, a definitive causal link between feedback energetics and the establishment/redshift evolution of the scaling relations has not been demonstrated, with alternative explanations (merger averaging, common gas supply) still viable.

status_evidence.title: Coevolution (Or Not) of Supermassive Black Holes and Host Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews observational scaling relations and notes ongoing debate about role of AGN feedback in their origin.
status_evidence.claim: The causal role of AGN feedback in establishing M_BH–host scaling relations remains debated.

status_evidence.title: Observational tests of AGN feedback (Harrison & Ramos Almeida)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent review concludes that linking observed AGN outflows to global host-galaxy regulation and to the BH–galaxy scaling relations is still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative impact of AGN feedback on scaling relations is still an open question.
